test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.**

David said, “Don’t worry Frank. I will bring you up to date when I meet you next.”

options.text: David told Frank not to worry as he would bring him up to date when he met him next.
David told Frank he shouldn’t worry as he will bring him up to date when he meets him next.
David told Frank not to worry as I would bring you up to date when I meet you next.
David told Frank don’t worry as he would bring you up to date when he met him next.

solution:
The correct answer is- 'David told Frank not to worry as he would bring him up to date when he met him next.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change the sentence to an **indirect speech **we need to **follow **the following steps:

 
 
• As the **reporting speech **is in the *past tense*, **said **will become **told**.
 
• The **inverted commas **of reported speech should be **removed**.
 
• As there is a **negative imperative sentence **(*Don't worry Frank*) so the sentence should start as "*not + to + verb*"
 
 
• *Not to worry. *(for the given sentence)
 
 
 
• The pronoun *I *will change to *he *(as it refers to the subject **David**)
 
• The pronoun *you *will change to *him *(as it refers to the object **Frank**)
 
 
 
• Thus according to the given steps, ***option 1 ***is the correct answer.

**And the correct sentence is:** *David told Frank not to worry as he would bring him up to date when he met him next*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Let's learn more about the change of tense in the reported speech:
 
 
• **Present Perfect **Changes to **Past Perfect**

 
 
• **Example:**

 
 
• Direct: *“I have been to Boston”, she told me.*
 
• Indirect: *She told me that she had been to Boston.*
 
 
 
 
 
• **Simple Present **Changes to **Simple Past**
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• Direct: *“I am unwell”, she said.*
 
• Indirect: *She said that she was unwell.*
 
 
 
 
 
• **Present Continuous **Changes to **Past Continuous**
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• Direct: *“I am playing the guitar”, she explained*.
 
• Indirect: *She explained that she was playing the guitar.*
 
 
 
 
 
• **Present Perfect **Changes to **Past Perfect**
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• Direct: *He said, “She has finished her homework“.*
 
• ​Indirect: *He said that she had finished her homework.*
